item.title: Myanmar: Is the US undermining the EU's diplomatic blockade?
item.description: With the US reopening talks with Myanmar's military-backed government, and several Southeast Asian countries restarting diplomatic contacts, the EU is facing uncomfortable questions about its own boycott of the junta.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Will elections in Israel change its Iran approach?
item.description: As Israelis head to the polls, the country's conflict with Iran casts a long shadow over the ballot box. But any leadership changes in Israel may not be enough to shake up its grand strategy on Tehran.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: A bad omen? Syria bans women from university courses
item.description: The recent announcement that Syrian tertiary institutes will not allow women into some courses has triggered debate. Critics worry it may be a sign that the new Syrian government is restricting women's rights.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Why Ukraine may be involved in Mali's conflict
item.description: Allegations that Ukrainian specialists are supporting Tuareg rebels in Mali highlight Kyiv's effort to challenge Russian influence far beyond the battlefield in Europe.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Germany's Merz in Asia as security issues loom large
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz will be meeting the leaders of Singapore, Japan and South Korea as Germany seeks to adjust its foreign policy to rising uncertainty and threats to global supply chains.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Venezuelan opposition leader Machado returns from exile
item.description: Nobel Peace Prize winner and popular Venezuelan political opposition figure Maria Corina Machado has returned after nearly a year away. Sitting President Rodriguez accused her of making a "show."
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Protein shakes for teenagers: Good or bad idea?
item.description: Protein products are marketed as a way of building muscle and losing weight — and they're very popular with young people. They also claim to promote healthy growth in children. Is this true? How much protein is healthy?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Uganda says it has no active Ebola cases, but infections in Kenya and Nigeria are prompting fresh scrutiny
item.description: Health officials are investigating whether Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria crossed paths at Uganda's main airport as conflicting accounts cloud the source of one infection.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Gadi Eisenkot campaigns on Moroccan roots in challenge to Netanyahu
item.description: As Israel prepares to vote, Gadi Eisenkot is leveraging his Moroccan heritage in Likud strongholds such as Sderot. From historical divides to October 7, identity and trauma are redefining the city's political loyalties.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
item.description: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.
